description: A button that stays pressed or unpressed, such as Bold in a text toolbar. It renders a real <button aria-pressed>.

aihio-toggle.description: Fired when the pressed state changes

handled: The component renders a real <button> with aria-pressed, so the role, Enter and Space activation, focus behaviour, disabled semantics, and the forced-colours mapping are the platform's rather than an emulation of them
aria-pressed on that control reflects the pressed attribute
aria-* set on the host is mirrored onto the control
The control is always type="button", so a toggle inside a form never submits it

required.requirement: Provide aria-label describing what the toggle controls (e.g. aria-label="Bold").

required.when: the toggle turns a setting on or off
required.requirement: Name the toggle after what it controls (e.g. "Bold"), never after its state: a toggle labelled "Enabled" is announced as "Enabled, toggle button, pressed" and never says what is enabled. For an on/off setting in a form, use aihio-switch.

counterExamples.reason: Nested interactives. Use aihio-toggle alone — it already renders a button.
Boolean attributes toggle on presence. Omit the attribute for unpressed; write `pressed` for pressed.

The toggle is named by its state and the visible label is not associated with it, so assistive technology announces "Enabled, toggle button, pressed" with no idea what is enabled. An on/off setting is a switch: use aihio-switch in aihio-field, which also submits with the form.

control.description: The native button delegated to by the component

pressed.description: Whether the toggle is pressed; reflects the pressed attribute

click().description: Activates the native button, toggling the pressed state.

focus().description: Moves focus to the native button.

blur().description: Removes focus from the native button.
